title: Bus passengers to be fined for playing loud music
speaker: Breaking News English (Sean Banville)

keyTerms.definition: money you must pay as a punishment
actions that annoy or upset other people in public
a person who travels to work or school
leaving rubbish on the ground in a public place

predictionQuestion: What annoys you on buses or trains? Should people be fined for it? What might the news say?

keyIdeas.text: Loud music on public transport annoys passengers who want to travel in quiet.
Singapore has introduced fines of up to S$500 for loud music on buses.
The fines also cover other anti-social behaviour, such as feet on seats, littering and eating on buses.
The government says the fines will make public transport safer and more pleasant, and every commuter has a part to play.
The government wants bus drivers to focus on driving safely.
But drivers can ask inconsiderate passengers to get off the bus.
Many commuters were happy with the new fines.
Example: a flight attendant who takes the bus to the airport was relieved.
Example: an older commuter just wants to get to work without other people's music.
